title: API and Database Integration
learning_outcomes: Explain the purpose of api and database integration in a C#/.NET program.
Predict the result of the included C# example and verify the documented output.
Apply api and database integration to a small task and identify one relevant boundary, limitation, or version requirement.

content.intro: API and Database Integration is lesson 156 in APIs, Networking, and Database Integration. Integration code should isolate network or database calls, use parameters instead of string-built commands, validate external data, and define transaction boundaries.
content.why_it_matters: External systems fail and return untrusted data, so integration code needs timeouts, validation, and clear data boundaries. This lesson focuses on api and database integration and shows how to verify the behavior instead of relying on assumptions.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Integration code should isolate network or database calls, use parameters instead of string-built commands, validate external data, and define transaction boundaries.

content_blocks.title: A practical way to learn it
content_blocks.text: Start with the smallest valid case for api and database integration. Predict the output, run or inspect the example in the stated toolchain, then change one input or rule and compare the result. For production code, record assumptions and verify boundary cases.

items.title: Separating application layers
items.text: Choose an approach from the problem and constraints; avoid adding abstraction without a concrete maintenance benefit.

items.title: Mapping data to objects
items.text: For mapping data to objects, define the expected behavior, inspect how it relates to api and database integration, and verify a representative case plus one boundary or failure case.

items.title: Validating input
items.text: Treat console input as text first; convert it only after a successful parse and show a useful recovery path.

items.title: Managing transactions
items.text: Treat HTTP and database responses as untrusted boundaries. Set timeouts, check status codes, parameterize SQL, validate deserialized results, and make transaction scope and disposal explicit.

items.title: Handling database failures
items.text: Use explicit timeouts, parameterized database commands, small service boundaries, and validation for external results.

items.title: Protecting sensitive information
items.text: For protecting sensitive information, define the expected behavior, inspect how it relates to api and database integration, and verify a representative case plus one boundary or failure case.

content.task: Try it yourself: create a small C# example that demonstrates api and database integration. Change one input or implementation detail, predict the result, then check it locally and explain one edge case.
task_acceptance_criteria: The example demonstrates api and database integration rather than only repeating its definition.
The result is checked locally or against a clearly documented reference output.
At least one relevant boundary, invalid-input case, or compatibility condition is considered.
hints: List the assumptions and expected behavior for api and database integration before editing the code.
Change one variable or rule at a time; keep the previous output for comparison.
If behavior differs, confirm the compiler/target framework and consult the linked official documentation.
content.solution_notes: Suggested approach: identify the expected input and output, start from the smallest example, use the feature only where it clarifies the rule, and verify both a typical case and a boundary/failure case.

common_mistakes.problem: Assuming the feature works identically on every target
common_mistakes.why: Language syntax, libraries, and runtime support are version-dependent.
common_mistakes.fix: Check the target framework and official versioned reference before using the feature.

common_mistakes.why: Boundary values, malformed input, and failure states often expose the real bug.
common_mistakes.fix: Add one typical input and one boundary or invalid case to the manual or automated checks.

common_mistakes.problem: Treating sample output as proof that the code ran
common_mistakes.why: The course reader uses static reference output for C# because it has no C# execution runner.
common_mistakes.fix: Run the snippet in a local .NET project or a separately isolated execution service.
